claims.text: A small, single alloying addition can promote in-situ precipitation of a lubricious secondary phase in CoCrFeNi.
The precipitated secondary phase will be uniformly distributed within the CoCrFeNi matrix.
The secondary phase will enable formation of a stable, self-renewing tribofilm during sliding.
The tribofilm will reduce interfacial shear and thereby lower friction and wear from room temperature to 800 °C.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy is homogeneous and single-phase.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy exhibits moderate friction.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy exhibits increasing wear rate as temperature rises.
The secondary phase will segregate to the sliding interface.
Segregation of the secondary phase will produce an adherent, continuous tribofilm.
The dopant-induced secondary phase has low shear strength.
The self-renewing tribofilm reduces adhesive contacts.
Reducing adhesive contacts through the tribofilm will reduce wear and maintain lower friction over the entire temperature range.
The modified alloy will have an approximately 20–30% lower coefficient of friction than baseline CoCrFeNi across the full range from room temperature to 800 °C.
The modified alloy will have a lower wear rate than baseline CoCrFeNi across the full range from room temperature to 800 °C.
The intervention will remain effective under moderate-to-high sliding loads in ambient atmosphere up to 800 °C.
The intervention's efficacy may diminish in environments that drastically alter oxidation.
The intervention's efficacy may diminish under extreme sliding loads beyond the tested range.
